statement: Let r=|Wa/G| and Omega be a unit cell. There exist r fixed G-invariant basis functions eta_i such that, for every f in C_G(R^2) and every epsilon>0, there exist h_i in C_Wa(R^2) whose unit-cell L1 approximation error is strictly below epsilon.
assumptions: G is a planar crystallographic group after the conjugation of Theorem 3.2
G is a subgroup of an affine reflection group Wa
Omega is one compact finite-measure unit cell
the Hironaka decomposition makes P_torus^G a free rank-[Wa:G] module over P_torus^Wa
trigonometric polynomials are uniformly dense in continuous periodic functions
pass_condition: Every symbolic proof obligation passes and three independent certificate corruptions are rejected.
noncircularity: No finite target or observed error selects the tolerance, basis count, or conclusion.
